hypothesis: Reuse the wall/separation graph built by joint-search overflow validation instead of reconstructing it inside each axis solve and unary probe.
prototype: Private repair_axis_prepared helper takes invocation-owned validated edges. Legacy public entry rebuilds normally; prepared edges are never reused after a separation flip. No cross-invocation cache or gate changes.
disposition: Rejected and production source restored. Eliminating duplicate graph construction did not improve end-to-end carrier model time in this A/B/A screen.

measurement.workload: Prepared carrier inputs, 165x159 mm, three runs per block, compact search, interior order 3, edge feasibility, owned quality and face cohesion, USB-JTAG contract-group candidates, board_aux owned-face-fixed/a2.2/owned-pins-forward, joint separation states 128.
measurement.interpretation: Prototype median is about 1.36% slower than initial baseline and 2.11% slower than reversed baseline. Small sequential samples, not a confidence interval; no speedup claim. Tests and audits finished before the measured prototype block.

correctness.joint_receipts: All joint_retry lines identical between initial and prototype blocks.

prototype_tests.native_floorplan_contracts: PASS 15.33s including independently rebuilt graph cross-check

correctness.retained_test: For every successful independent-oracle fixture, rebuild both selected axis graphs through the standalone repair API and compare their positions against the joint solution.

scope: C++ implementation experiment only; no Python comparison, new full board qualification or smaller-board claim.
next: Prioritise larger measured costs, especially source-audit AST projection, rather than accumulating solver micro-optimisations with no demonstrated end-to-end benefit.
